summary: The 2026 Iran war (the US and Israel against Iran, since Feb 28) is in a tense pause: President Trump and Secretary of State Rubio say new strikes are unlikely or not needed while the US blockade of Iran continues, and Qatar says it sees progress in mediation. Iran denies that talks are under way and says the Strait of Hormuz stays shut to unapproved shipping until its conditions are met; attacks on tankers in and near the strait continued on Nov 10, and Iran's army said a tanker caught fire in the strait after hitting a mine on Nov 11. On Nov 11 Iran's parliament speaker said the strait will never return to its pre-war status, while President Trump said the US has already won and wants a total victory.

status.label: Strait of Hormuz
status.note: Iran says it is closed to ships that don't coordinate with its Persian Gulf Strait Authority; the US says the main routes are controlled by the US and its regional partners. Most traffic moves through a shuttle system the US coordinates with Arab partners, with weekly volumes swinging as attacks continue (Al Jazeera).

status.label: Oil through Hormuz
status.note: About 11.6 million barrels a day over the seven days to Oct 13, about 68% of the 17.1 million pre-war baseline (Kpler, via Al Jazeera).

status.label: The war
status.note: US officials said the US carried out limited, defensive strikes on Iranian targets, including on Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz on Nov 2, after Iranian surface-to-air missile threats; they said it was not a resumption of major combat (Wall Street Journal, then Reuters). Indirect talks through Qatari mediators continue with no breakthrough announced; Vice President Vance said there has been progress. On Nov 7 the US carried out further strikes on Iranian air defences on Qeshm Island, which President Trump called minor (Euronews). On Nov 8 Trump told CNN renewed attacks were highly unlikely if talks make real progress; no deal has been signed.

status.label: Brent crude
status.note: Brent was up 52 cents at US$92.01 a barrel by 7:30 GMT on Wednesday, Nov 11 (2:30 a.m. ET), rebounding from a two-month low as attacks on Hormuz shipping blunted hopes for a truce (Reuters, via Sowetan and Business Recorder).

updates.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said two supertankers were disabled by explosions on Wednesday night after ignoring warnings against an unauthorised route, and Iran's army said two more tankers hit mines in the eastern strait on Thursday afternoon. Reuters said it could not immediately verify Iran's account; UKMTO reported a vessel hit by an unidentified projectile about 14 nautical miles northwest of Ras Al-Khaimah on Wednesday, with all crew evacuated.
sources: Reuters via GV Wire: Four tankers struck by explosions in Strait of Hormuz, Iran says
AFP via Gulf Today: Two oil tankers 'disabled' by explosions in Strait of Hormuz

updates.text: President Trump said on Nov 12 that the US does not need a deal with Iran; no agreement has been announced and the blockade continues.
sources: ABC News live: 'We don't need a deal with Iran,' Trump says
Haaretz: Trump says Iran deal is no longer needed

updates.text: Iran's IRGC Navy said it struck Didamar (Little Quoin) Island, an uninhabited Omani island in the Strait of Hormuz, saying it was used to help enemy oil shipments; Reuters sources said navigation and communications equipment was hit, and Oman confirmed a loud explosion there.
sources: Fox News / Reuters: Iran claims strike on Omani island
Just The News: Iran strikes Omani island

updates.text: Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said on Nov 11 that the Strait of Hormuz will never return to its pre-war status and that Iran will not back down.
sources: Al Jazeera: Hormuz Strait will 'never return' to pre-war status, Iran's Ghalibaf says
Iran International live: Ghalibaf says Iran will not back down

updates.text: President Trump said on Nov 11 that the US has already won the war with Iran and that he wants a total victory; no agreement has been announced.
sources: Times of Israel live blog, Nov 11
Iran International live: Trump seeks 'total victory'

updates.text: Iran's army said an oil tanker was on fire in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting a mine; Iran's IRGC Navy said mines struck two tankers in the strait.

Data from the Washington Institute for Near East Policy show 37 ships were attacked in and near the Strait of Hormuz in October, the most in any month since the war began, with little sign of fewer attacks in November (Reuters).

After the G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris on Nov 10, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the economic campaign against Iran is so damaging that there is currently no need for major combat operations.

background: The war began on Feb 28, 2026 with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. An April ceasefire collapsed on July 8. The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April (reinstated in July); Iran restricts and attacks shipping through Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war.
factcheck: Checked by Claude against at least two reputable sources where possible. Statements by Iran's military, the US military (CENTCOM) or President Trump are labelled as claims, because each side's account of who controls the strait differs.
